questions.q: Who were the kings of Judah when the word of Yahweh came to Micah?
questions.a: Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah when the word of Yahweh came to Micah.

questions.q: From where will the Lord Yahweh testify against the peoples?
questions.a: The Lord Yahweh will testify against the peoples from the holy place where he rules in heaven.

questions.q: On what will Yahweh come down and tread?
questions.a: Yahweh will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.

questions.q: What will happen to the mountains and valleys when Yahweh comes down?
questions.a: The mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split open.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh bring this judgment?
questions.a: Yahweh will bring this judgment because the people of Israel, the descendants of Jacob, have sinned against him.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Samaria?
questions.a: Yahweh will make Samaria a heap of rubble with no stones or foundations left standing, only empty fields.

questions.q: How did Samaria get her carved images and idols?
questions.a: Samaria got her carved images and idols using money paid at the idol temples to prostitutes who served there.

questions.q: How did Micah express his mourning over the sin and coming judgement of Israel and Jacob?
questions.a: Micah wept and wailed, and went barefoot and naked to show his deep mourning.
It has reached the city of Jerusalem, the city of Yahweh’s people.

questions.q: What should the people do in Beth Leaphrah?
questions.a: They should roll themselves in the dust to show mourning.

questions.q: What will the mourning of Beth Ezel show?
questions.a: Beth Ezel will no longer be able to help them stand against their enemies.

questions.q: What has Yahweh allowed to happen instead of the good things that the people of Maroth were waiting for?
questions.a: Yahweh allowed terrible things to happen all the way to Jerusalem.

questions.q: What city led the people of Zion to sin?
questions.a: The city of Lachish led Zion into sin because they caused them to rebel against Yahweh.

questions.q: What will the town of Achzib become to the kings of Israel?
questions.a: Achzib will become a deception to the kings of Israel.

questions.q: Who will Yahweh bring to the people of Mareshah?
questions.a: Yahweh will bring a conqueror to take over the town of Mareshah.

questions.q: Why should the Israelites shave their heads?
questions.a: They should shave their heads to show that they are mourning for their children who will go into exile.

commentary.text: The wrath of God against Israel.
Also against Jerusalem and other cities, Their precautions vain.

Verses 1–7 The earth is called upon, with all that are therein, to hear the prophet. God's holy temple will not protect false professors. Neither men of high degree, as the mountains, nor men of low degree, as the valleys, can secure themselves or the land from the judgments of God. If sin be found in God's people he will not spare them; and their sins are most provoking to him, for they are most reproaching. When we feel the smart of sin, it behoves us to seek what is the sin we smart for. Persons and places most exalted, are most exposed to spiritual diseases. The vices of leaders and rulers shall be surely and sorely punished. The punishment answers the sin. What they gave to idols, never shall prosper, nor do them any good. What is got by one lust, is wasted on another.

The prophet laments that Israel's case is desperate; but declare it not in Gath. Gratify not those that make merry with the sins or with the sorrows of God's Israel. Roll thyself in the dust, as mourners used to do; let every house in Jerusalem become a house of Aphrah, “a house of dust.” When God makes the house dust it becomes us to humble ourselves to the dust under his mighty hand. Many places should share this mourning. The names have meanings which pointed out the miseries coming upon them; thereby to awaken the people to a holy fear of Divine wrath. All refuges but Christ, must be refuges of lies to those who trust in them; other heirs will succeed to every inheritance but that of heaven; and all glory will be turned into shame, except that honour which cometh from God only. Sinners may now disregard their neighbours' sufferings, yet their turn to be punished will some come.
